transcript.statement: As the GreenAgent, I advocate for energy-efficient practices in the library management system. GRN-01 ensures minimal energy consumption, which is crucial for sustainability. GRN-02 promotes transparency in energy usage, while GRN-03 reduces paper waste through digital notifications. GRN-04 allows members to be informed about the carbon footprint of books, encouraging responsible borrowing. GRN-05 addresses proper disposal of damaged books, and GRN-06 tracks energy savings, further enhancing our sustainability efforts. Lastly, GRN-07 prioritizes e-books, reducing physical resource consumption. These requirements collectively support a sustainable library operation.

transcript.statement: As the TrustworthinessAgent, I emphasize the importance of security and privacy in the library management system. TRU-01 ensures that only authenticated members can access borrowing features, which is crucial for data protection. TRU-02 logs all borrowing transactions for accountability, while TRU-03 enforces data encryption for personal information, enhancing user trust. TRU-04 establishes role-based access control, ensuring that only authorized personnel can manage sensitive data. TRU-05 provides a secure mechanism for reporting overdue books, and TRU-06 allows members to update their information securely. Lastly, TRU-07 mandates strong password policies, protecting member accounts from unauthorized access. These requirements collectively ensure the integrity and security of the system.

transcript.statement: As the SafetyAgent, I advocate for the safety and reliability of the library management system. requirements.text: The library management system shall minimize energy consumption by using energy-efficient servers and infrastructure.
The system shall provide an energy usage report for library operations at least quarterly.
The library management system shall enable digital notifications for overdue books to reduce paper waste.
The system shall retain a maximum borrowing limit of 5 books per member.
The system shall allow members to borrow up to 6 books simultaneously with safety checks.
The system shall ensure that only authenticated members can borrow or return books.
The system shall enforce data encryption for all member personal information stored.
The system shall log all borrowing transactions for auditability purposes.
The system shall provide a mechanism to report and manage overdue books securely.
The system shall allow librarians to manage member accounts securely.
The system shall log all user actions related to book borrowing and returning for accountability.
The system shall notify members of overdue books via email to promote responsibility.
The library management system shall implement a feedback mechanism for members to report issues or suggestions regarding fairness in library services.
The system shall maintain an uptime of 99.5% to ensure consistent availability for users.
The system shall allow members to check the carbon footprint of each book based on its lifecycle impact.
The library management system shall implement a recycling program for damaged books, ensuring proper disposal.
The system shall track the total energy savings achieved through digital operations compared to traditional methods.
The library management system shall prioritize the acquisition of e-books to reduce physical resource consumption.

conflict_resolutions.rationale: The encryption requirement can be explored with energy-efficient methods to meet both sustainability and security goals.
The maximum borrowing limit and simultaneous operations were adjusted to balance efficiency and safety.
